needsYou.title: Your line options are built and measured — and option C does not actually do anything
needsYou.productImpact:
You asked to see both before picking. Both are built and photographed on the real page, in both themes — and measuring them turned up two things worth a minute before you point.

FIRST: option C was "keep the colour, make it thicker". It does not work. Making a line wider does not change its colour, and the colour is the entire reason you could not see it — that line differs from the card behind it by 19 shades out of 255. At two pixels it is still 19 shades. It is a thicker invisible line. I would rather tell you that than ship it and let you find out.

SECOND: you were told "darker cannot be done inside the line colours". That was wrong. Whoever wrote it stopped at the five border colours and did not look further down the same list, where there are six more, getting steadily darker. So there is a THIRD option nobody offered you, and it is the one I would choose: still a line, but three times the difference.

Option B — the text grey — works too: five times the difference. It is unmistakable, and slightly heavier than the thing it is joining.
needsYou.workedExample:
The line is the short vertical connector between two alert rows on Admin → Overview — 1 pixel wide, 8 to 14 pixels tall, joining one alert's icon to the next. There are eleven on your page right now.

How far each option is from the card behind it, out of 255:

  today            19
  C  thicker       19   ← unchanged, that is the point
  D  darker line   55
  B  text grey     95

In dark mode: 16 today, 16 for C, 57 for D, 110 for B.

On the sheets in your gallery, top to bottom: today and C both read as nothing. B and D both read as a real connector.

needsYou.title: One of your two staff-frame rulings needs a second word — "darker" has nowhere to go
needsYou.productImpact:
You gave two rulings on the admin frames: the admin role pill gets colour, and the faint line between alert rows should be DARKER because you could not see it. The first is unambiguous and is queued.

The second has no obvious next step, and I would rather ask than guess. That line uses the lightest of five border colours, and all five sit inside about 2% of each other — in light mode the range is #ECECEE to #E4E4E7, which is eight steps out of 255. Moving it to the darkest one would be invisible. In DARK mode the first two are literally the same colour, so a change there would do nothing at all.

So "darker" cannot be satisfied inside the border palette. It needs either a properly darker grey from the text palette — a different kind of line, more visible than any border on the page — or the line stays its colour and gets thicker instead.

⚠ ANSWERED — you said "Show me both, then I'll pick". Both are built and photographed. ⚠ And two corrections to what this card told you, because they change the choice: the claim that darker could not be done inside the line colours was WRONG (whoever wrote it stopped at the five border colours and did not look further down the same list), and one of the two options turns out not to work. The pick is now its own card below.
needsYou.workedExample:
The line in question is the short vertical connector between two alert rows on Admin → Overview: it is 1 pixel wide and between 8 and 14 pixels tall, joining one alert's icon to the next.

An earlier shift measured that the lines genuinely exist at that size and still could not see them in its own screenshots — which matches what you said.

If it goes to a text grey it will read as a deliberate timeline, closer to a thin rule than to a border. If it gets thicker instead it stays a hairline in character and just becomes findable.
needsYou.recommendation:
My recommendation is to see it rather than decide it in words: next shift builds both versions and puts one frame in front of you with the two side by side, and you point. It is ten minutes and it removes the guessing.

Nothing is blocked meanwhile — the admin pill half of that card can ship on its own.

⚠ DONE: you chose (a), both were built, and the admin pill shipped the same night. The pick is the next card.

The reviewer DOES have a manual road today (adding a label to the pull request), and the button the card asked for cannot carry a review at all: the tool the reviewer runs on supports being started that way but is then given no pull request to attach its answer to, so it would run and post nothing. So the choice is: (A) write that down as the recipe and leave the new button alone until the reviewer is back and it can actually be tested, or (B) build the button anyway in the different mode that would be needed.

eyeItems.title: The requests waiting on you are on the bar of every admin page now — and one frame shows why it nearly shipped wrong
eyeItems.question:
You asked for two things on 1 September and both are live.

THE FIRST: "if mods sent 5 requests to the admin panel it shold show 5 requests pending". The number now sits on the Change requests tab, on every admin page — not just the dashboard. Five waiting draws a 5; none waiting draws nothing at all, rather than a (0).

THE SECOND: "even thought crew has its own refresh principles should we just fold it into the same as overview so everything is consistent". The line at the foot no longer says when it last checked — the bar says that — but it still tells you WHO wrote the briefing, which is the more useful half.

ONE THING WORTH KNOWING, because it is a real change to how this page behaves: Crew used to re-read itself every minute no matter what. It now follows the panel-wide AUTO switch, which is ON by default — so nothing changes for you unless you turn AUTO off, and then Crew stops re-reading itself like every other page, with the refresh button right there.

THE LAST FRAME IS THE ONE I WOULD LOOK AT. It is the bug the reviewer caught before this shipped: decline requests on the requests page and the list empties while the bar still says 5. Fixed, and the frame is kept because a picture of the bar contradicting the page in the same screenshot is the clearest statement of why one number must have one source.

eyeItems.title: One switch for the whole panel — and the page you cited as correct was never doing it either
eyeItems.question:
You asked why the refresh controls act as individual toggles per admin page, and said it should work the way the moderator pages work. It does now. But the reason it was broken is not the reason it looked broken, and that decided the fix.

THE MODERATOR PAGE WAS NEVER SHARING ANYTHING.

It looks like it holds the switch across everything you do because /moderator is ONE page — its tabs are inside it, so nothing ever unloads. The admin panel is EIGHT separate pages, and each one loaded a fresh switch set to off. Neither side had any shared setting at all; seven pages each kept their own private copy. So copying the moderator page would have been copying nothing. What has been built is the thing neither side had.

WHAT YOU SHOULD SEE.

Turn AUTO 30s on anywhere — Overview, Users, Change requests, Invite codes, Bug reports, Audit logs, or the moderator dashboard — and walk anywhere else. It is on. Turn it off and that travels too. Close the browser and come back tomorrow and it is still how you left it.

⚠ ONE DECISION IS YOURS, AND I HAVE MADE A CALL YOU MAY WANT TO REVERSE.

One shared switch means one starting position, and the eight pages disagreed about it: Overview started ON, the other seven started OFF. I looked up why Overview was different, expecting a decision of yours — it was not. It came from the original scaffolding commit back when that page was first built, so nobody ever chose it.

I have set the shared starting position to ON, because that way no page loses anything it did today and you get what you asked for without clicking. The cost is that five admin pages now re-read themselves every 30 seconds when they used not to. The alternative is OFF, where nothing starts polling that did not before, but your landing page stops refreshing on arrival the way it always has.

Either way it remembers you the moment you touch it, and it is one line to flip. Say the word if you want OFF.

THE FRAMES BELOW ARE THE SAME PAGE, NOTHING CLICKED.

Both are /admin/users reached by clicking Users from Overview. On the left of each pair is how it is now, on the right how it was this morning.

frames.caption: Walked here from Overview without touching the switch. AUTO is on, because it is the same switch.
The same walk this morning. One navigation and the switch is off again — this is exactly what you were looking at when you wrote.
The same thing in the light theme.
And how it was, in the light theme.

eyeItems.title: The missing refresh controls — and your question found twice what the card did
eyeItems.question:
You asked why only some admin pages carry "the updated time the auto refresh toggle and a notification button". They all do now. But the interesting part is what turned up on the way, and it is worth two minutes.

THE CARD SAID TWO PAGES WERE WRONG. FOUR WERE.

Whoever wrote the card searched the pages for the setting that draws those controls and found two pages missing it — Invite codes and Bug reports. That search was answering a slightly different question than yours. Users and Change requests HAD the setting, and inside it they had only the refresh button — no time, no toggle. So they matched the search and still failed two of the three things you named. The first frame below is the Users page as it was: one lonely refresh icon and nothing else.

THE REASON THOSE TWO PAGES GAVE FOR IT WAS SIMPLY WRONG.

Each had a note in the code saying the missing pieces were "state no reader produces" — meaning the page had nothing to show, so showing nothing was correct. That is false. Every one of these pages already knows the moment its data arrived, and the Overview page has been reading exactly that since these bars were built. Nobody had ever asked it. I corrected the design brief that note was citing, because the brief is what the next person reads.

WHAT YOU WILL SEE

Open Invite codes, Bug reports, Users or Change requests. Same three things Overview has, same place, same behaviour. Bug reports is the one that matters most — it is an inbox, a row only appears when a customer somewhere hits Report a bug, and until now the only way to find out one had arrived was to leave the page and come back.

ONE THING I DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO

The card told me to write a note in the code explaining that the Crew page is permanently different. I did not, because you reversed that yourself the same day on another card — you asked whether Crew should just fold into the same refresh as everything else, and the answer there is yes. Writing a paragraph defending an exception on the day you have asked to remove it is a document that is stale before it is saved. Instead a test now goes red the moment Crew is folded in, so that night has to delete Crew's own "checked 2 minutes ago" line at the same time — otherwise the page would tell you how fresh it is twice.

HOW HARD I LOOKED

All eight staff pages, both light and dark, driven in a real browser: 106 readings, none wrong. Then the same run against the old code as a control: 20 failures, in exactly the shape described above. The toggle is clicked rather than just looked at, because a switch that draws two states and changes neither is the sort of thing that ships looking finished.

The photographs below are dark; light was measured the same way with the same result.

frames.caption: The Users page as it was. One refresh icon, no time, no toggle — and the card's own search reported this page as correct, because the setting was there and two thirds of it was empty.
The same page now: the time it was last read, the AUTO 30s switch, and the refresh button. The same three things Overview has, in the same place.
Bug reports had nothing at all. This is the inbox a customer's report lands in, and there was no way to see whether one had arrived without leaving the page.
The same bar now. With AUTO on it re-reads every 30 seconds, so a report that arrives while you are looking at the page shows up without you doing anything.

eyeItems.title: You can see which account you are looking into — before and after, side by side
eyeItems.question:
You said the open profile was "all one color" and you could not tell which row you were in. It is fixed, and the before/after pair below is the whole story: same table, same account, same moment in both.

It landed in ONE place. Every admin and moderator table draws the same shared component, so one change reached all twelve — the Users table you were looking at, audit logs, invite codes, bug reports, change requests, blocked IPs, flagged referrals, the moderator's own lists. No individual page was touched, which is exactly what that shared component was built for.

TWO THINGS I OWE YOU, and the second is the more useful one.

FIRST — the shading was not safe on its own. There was a note in the code from the last time this came up saying a shaded row would swallow the evidence block, the box that holds a customer's own words on a bug report or a moderator's reasoning on a request. That note was RIGHT. So the evidence box stopped being a shaded box and became an outlined one, and it is legible on the new ground. Have a look at the third frame below — that is a real bug report on the new ground.

SECOND — the prototype does not actually solve this, and I only found that by opening it rather than trusting the screenshot. It paints the open row, the hover, and the evidence box all the SAME single colour. Your frame looked right because the account you had open was active, and the prototype draws no evidence box for an active account, so the collision never showed. The look it is telling us is right; the value is not. Ours keeps the three apart: resting, hover one step lighter, open two.

This also reverses the answer you gave me on #396 ("The expansion reads fine — no change"). That is written into the code beside the change, with the arms to stop a future night quietly putting the flat row back because it read your older reply first.

You asked me to check every relevant admin and moderator page. I opened all twelve with a row expanded, in both light and dark — 289 readings, none of them wrong. Five of them had no rows at all in the test database, so I put test rows in rather than tell you a page was fine without looking at it.

The same row, the same account. The open row and its whole expansion are one lighter block; the closed rows around it are not. Slightly different, as you asked — findable at a glance rather than a slab of colour.

frames.caption: A real bug report opened on the new ground. The customer's own words sit in an outlined box rather than a shaded one — this is the half that makes the shading safe, and without it that box would have disappeared into the row behind it.

eyeItems.title: The long list of finished work is gone, and the empty section now says what it is for
eyeItems.question:
You asked whether ALREADY DEALT WITH and NOT DONE YET were sections you even needed. I measured both before answering, and they turned out to be in opposite states — so the answer is different for each, and the numbers are the reason.

ALREADY DEALT WITH was drawing 281 rows. It was the FOURTH place this page told you something was finished: WORKING NOW names the last shifts and what each shipped, THE PROGRAM ticks a milestone's steps as they land, and that block listed everything, forever. It is gone.

NOT DONE YET was drawing NOTHING, because every one of its 163 rows had already merged — and that is the argument for KEEPING it. It is the only place on this page a piece of work shows up that is blocked, or waiting on you, or in review, and is not in NEXT UP and not a milestone step. Delete it and that work is invisible until someone happens to open GitHub, which is exactly what happened to you before.

So what it needed was not deleting, it was an honest empty line. It used to say "Nothing is in flight. Everything the crew has started has landed." — which describes the rows and teaches you nothing. It now says "Nothing is stuck. Blocked work and anything waiting on you appears here." The second sentence is the point: an empty box should tell you what a FULL one would mean, otherwise "nothing is stuck" and "this section is broken" look identical.

Nothing was thrown away. Every merged row and every answered card is still in the file behind this page, and that file is in version control.

Worth two minutes: scroll to the bottom of this page. It is shorter, and the third frame shows you what NOT DONE YET will look like the next time something actually is stuck.

The same modal tonight. "File a request", the app's own dark surface, and every field legible. Submit is grey because the form is empty, which is what it always did.
Suspend a user, dark mode, last night. Same white box. Note the confirm button is a washed pink — the disabled state of a red that was written into the file rather than taken from the palette.

The same dialog tonight. The red here is the palette's one red and it is deliberate: suspension logs somebody out and keeps them out. This is the treatment I would most like you to check — four actions wear it and everything else now wears black.

And light mode, so the fix is not just a dark-mode patch. Every one of these dialogs was hard-coded light before, so light is the theme that should look UNCHANGED — if anything here reads differently to you, that is the thing to say.

eyeItems.title: Reconciliation now leads with the answer — is the discrepancy where your eye goes first?
eyeItems.question: Your brief said the pane ran backwards: a banner, two dense columns, then a six-row table whose LAST line was the discrepancy — "the answer to the entire view, in 12px, at the bottom." It is now a 30px figure directly under the account, and I measured that nothing else on the surface is bigger. What I want your eye on is whether the number you came for is genuinely the first thing you land on, and whether stripping five colours out has made the page harder to scan rather than easier — it is the sharpest version of the colour rule in the product, so it is the one most likely to have gone too far.

frames.caption: Moderation last night, in dark mode. White cards inside a dark app, blue/green/amber tints on ordinary numbers, an Actions column whose only button did what clicking the row already did — and every row of LAST ACTIVE reading "Never", which it has done for every account since the column was built.
The same page tonight. Click an account and its investigation opens underneath it at full width — that is what made room for the verdict. THE LEDGERS AGREE, with the discrepancy at 30px on the right.

The same thing in light. Worth a moment on "Total spent 0" — it read "−0" until I looked at a frame. Twenty-nine tests and ninety-four browser checks had passed over a negative zero printed in a ledger.

The evidence below the verdict: label, spacer, figure in mono, a hairline before each subtotal. The discrepancy row that used to sit at the bottom of this card is deleted — it is the verdict, and saying it twice is the double-count your Crew work removed.

eyeItems.title: Crew in dark mode — does the before/after read the way you expected?

None of those moved, and there are tests holding each one. What I want your eye on is whether the page still reads like a briefing rather than a dashboard, and whether the eye gallery breaking out to the wider measure is the right call at your screen size.

frames.caption: Crew last night, in dark mode. The page is a white sheet inside a dark app — Crew had never been dark-tested, and this is what that looked like.

The same page in light mode, so the change is a theme rather than a repaint.

eyeItems.title: The dashboard leads with what needs you, and almost nothing is coloured (brief 07)
eyeItems.question:
WHAT YOU ARE LOOKING AT. Five frames from tonight, both themes, plus the banner form.

THE ONE THING TO TRY. Open Admin. The first thing on the page is NEEDS A HUMAN with the three things actually waiting. Then imagine the day nothing is waiting — that whole section is simply not there, and the page starts at LAST 24 HOURS. That was your instruction and it is the strongest thing this page now does, but it is the one thing a screenshot cannot show you, because today there are three items to show.

WHAT I AM ASKING. Three judgements, none of them a bug:

1. THE CREDIT CHART HAS TWO GREY LINES. Purchased is black, consumed is mid-grey. Your rule is that the accent colour means something needs attention — and credits being bought and spent is the business working, not a fault, so neither line earned it. The cost is that the two lines are told apart by darkness rather than by hue. If that reads as too subtle, say so; it is a rule I applied rather than a look I chose.

2. THE PLAN BAR IS A GREY LADDER. Free, Starter, Pro, Enterprise used to be grey, blue, purple and black. They are four steps of one grey now, darkest first, with the legend naming each. Same argument: a plan is not an emergency.

3. THE ALERT ROWS ARE JOINED BY A HAIRLINE you can barely see. That is the colour your brief specified, and I measured that the lines are really there — 8 to 14 pixels each. But I could not see them in my own screenshots, which usually means a reader will not either.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY STILL UGLY, AND IT IS THE SECOND NIGHT I HAVE SAID IT. The five staff dialogs — suspend, freeze, adjust credits, change role, review — are still light-only, so opening one in dark mode gives you a white box. No brief owns them. It has now been reported twice, which is the point at which it should probably become a card of its own rather than a paragraph in mine.

frames.caption: Admin Overview in light. NEEDS A HUMAN first, with dashed cards — dashed means not yet — then the four numbers. Only the dots are coloured, because only they are urgent.

The same page in dark, and the chart follows it. This is the bit your brief called most likely to be missed: on main that line is emerald in BOTH themes, because the colour was written into the code rather than read from the theme.
The alerts list, light. Every row now reads as words — "Credits · admin added" — where before nine of these twelve showed the raw code name. Full width, so nothing is cut off at 280 pixels any more.
The same list in dark. The critical row at the top is the only thing wearing red; everything else identifies itself with an icon and its name.
The banner form. The chosen type is the filled one — which sounds obvious, and was broken: the selected chip had no styling at all, so all four looked identical. Found by checking, not by testing.

eyeItems.title: Twelve staff lists on one table, and the row opens where you clicked it (brief 06)
eyeItems.question:
WHAT YOU ARE LOOKING AT. Five frames from tonight, both themes.

THE ONE THING TO TRY. Open Admin → Users, click a row, and act on it. The row opens underneath itself and everything above and below stays on screen, so when you close it the next person is where they were. That is the entire argument for this change and it does not read from a screenshot — it reads from doing it twice.

WHAT I AM ASKING. Three judgements, and none of them is a bug:

1. The expansion opens with a hairline and a rise, and the row keeps its background. I tried it with a shaded background instead and the evidence block — which sits on the shade — disappeared into it. If it reads as not-obviously-open to you, that is the thing to say.

2. Status pills carry colour ONLY where somebody needs to act — suspended, frozen, locked, failed. Everything at rest is grey, and so is every role, including admin, which used to be purple. On a page where everything is coloured, nothing is; but you may want admin loud.

3. The counts above each table follow the same rule, so Suspended and Locked only go red when they are not zero. A red "0 SUSPENDED" was the loudest thing on the page saying nothing was wrong.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY STILL UGLY. The dialogs — suspend, freeze, credits — are untouched and still light-only, so opening one in dark mode gives you a white box. No brief owns them yet; they are counted and on the record rather than half-fixed inside a table brief.

frames.caption: Admin → Users in dark, with a row open. The six counts are grey because nothing needs acting on; FROZEN carries colour, ACTIVE and every role do not.
The same page in light. One flexible column (the person), everything else at a fixed width — which is what makes twelve different tables look like one table.
Moderation → Audit logs in dark, a row open: the facts grid, then the raw payload, then the actions with the consequence sentence beside them. This page had never been looked at in dark mode.
Change requests. The four coloured count tiles are gone — they were a SECOND filter for the same state as the filter row, and their numbers are the filter's own labels now.
Invite codes at 1024, dark. Nothing scrolls sideways at any width — the columns give way instead of hiding behind an edge.

eyeItems.title: Admin and Moderation now live inside the studio instead of replacing it (brief 05)
eyeItems.question:
WHAT YOU ARE LOOKING AT. Five frames from tonight's build.

THE CHANGE IN ONE SENTENCE. Opening Admin used to take the whole app away — the rail vanished, the topbar vanished, your account menu and credits chip vanished, and you landed on a grey page with a small "Studio" button in the corner to get back. It read like a different product. Staff is now a surface inside Klieg: same rail, same topbar, same account menu, with one bar across the top carrying the section tabs. There is no "Studio" button any more, because the rail is always there.

THE PAGES THEMSELVES ARE UNTOUCHED, ON PURPOSE. Not one table, card, chart, modal or query changed. That is your own brief's acceptance test — "same data, same actions, same everything, new frame" — so the insides still look dated inside the new frame. Briefs 06 to 09 fix them one at a time, and they are all unblocked now.

THE ONE THING WORTH TWO MINUTES. Open Audit logs and scroll. The bar does not move. Staff pages are working tools and the audit table runs to thousands of rows, so the tabs stay where you left them rather than scrolling off the top. Measured: the bar's top held at 56 pixels while the table moved 1,475.

WHAT YOUR BRIEF COULD NOT KNOW. It names one header to replace. There were two — Moderation had its own copy, with its own "Studio" button and its own Live/Paused pair. Renaming just the one you named would have left Moderation wearing two headers stacked on top of each other, and nothing would have flagged it. Both are gone.

THE HONEST BIT. In dark mode a staff page is a dark frame around white cards. The frame follows the theme; the content inside it never has, because staff has never been dark-tested. That is not something tonight broke — it is something tonight made visible, and it is exactly what 06 to 09 are for. The 134 hard-coded light colours are counted page by page and written down rather than quietly fixed, because your brief said to log them.

frames.caption: Admin Overview, dark. The rail and topbar are there; ADMIN / "Klieg Studio — everything" sits left, seven tabs beside it, and the auto-refresh switch replaces the old filled black Live/Paused button.
The same page in light. The tab labels are sentence case now — "Audit logs", not "Audit Logs" — matching the rest of the product.
Moderation. Its five sections are in the bar with their counts, and "New Request" keeps the filled button — that is a real action, which is what a filled button is for.
Crew reads at your narrower 790px measure rather than the 1240px the other surfaces use — a briefing you read, not a grid you scan.
At 1024 the bar wraps onto two rows and keeps every tab reachable. Nothing hides behind a sideways scrollbar.

eyeItems.title: Change plan, before and after - the annual toggle used to look like a tenfold price rise
eyeItems.question:
WHAT YOU ARE LOOKING AT. Five frames. Two of them are the live studio today; three are tonight's build.

START WITH THE ANNUAL PAIR. On the live studio, switching to Annual turns "$159 / month" into "$1,584 / year" - beside a badge promising 2 MONTHS FREE. Both numbers are correct and the pair is unreadable: the price appears to multiply by ten at the moment we claim to be saving you money, and there is nothing on screen you could divide to check it. On the new one it reads "$132 / month" with "billed yearly" beneath. Same charge, said in the unit everything else on the card uses.

THEN THE CARD ITSELF. The Upgrade button has moved up, between the price and the credits - it used to be last, under four lines of detail, furthest from the number it is answering. The tick reading "Every model and every tool" is gone from all three cards and appears once underneath: a fact true of every plan cannot help you choose between them, so it was taking up space three times over. And the little grey figure by the plan name is the other way up - "3,145 CREDITS PER $1", which climbs as you go up the ladder, instead of "0.036¢ a credit", where our twelve plans only differ in the third decimal.

THE COMPARE PAIR. Same table, and two things changed: the price row keeps its label - it says "Price a month" whichever toggle you are on, because a comparison whose unit moves under you is not a comparison - and the value row is inverted like the cards.

WHAT TO JUDGE: whether the annual price reads honestly, whether the button in the middle is better than the button at the bottom, and whether "3,145 CREDITS PER $1" is clearer than "0.036¢ A CREDIT". Nothing here changes what you are charged, which plans exist, or what any of them cost.

frames.caption: BEFORE - annual on the live studio: "$1,584 / year" beside a 2 MONTHS FREE badge, the button last, the same tick on all three cards.
AFTER - annual on tonight's build: "$132 / month" with "billed yearly", the Upgrade button between price and credits, one footnote instead of three ticks.
AFTER - the monthly view, for the shape of the card: name and value figure, price, action, then what the credits are and what they make.
BEFORE - compare mode on annual: the row label flips to "Price a year" and the totals jump, so the columns stop being comparable to the cards.
AFTER - compare mode on annual: "Price a month" stays put, "Credits per dollar" climbs left to right, and the footer button reads "$311 / mo" rather than a year's total.

eyeItems.title: Your Usage pane, before and after — and the reason it said zero is not the reason anyone expected
eyeItems.question:
WHAT YOU ARE LOOKING AT. Two pairs and one single. First pair: the Usage pane on the live studio, then on tonight's build. Second pair: the Refer a friend footer, the same way. Last one: Profile, where Remove now works.

THE THING WORTH TWO MINUTES, and it is the diagnosis rather than the fix. You said Usage was showing you had used no credits. It was — and the sum was RIGHT. Your last paid roll was 30 August. The month rolled over on 1 September. The pane was adding up "this month", and this month, at the moment you looked, genuinely had nothing in it. Adding harder would have given you the same zero.

So there was nothing wrong with the arithmetic and two things wrong with the WINDOW. Your account has no billing period at all — it is a free plan, so there is no monthly cycle recorded against it — and the pane invented a calendar month to stand in for one. Worse, the "of 5,000 this month" it measured you against does not exist: a free account's credits are handed over once, at signup, and NOTHING ever tops them back up. That line was promising you a refill that never comes.

It now says what it actually knows. Where there is a real billing period it uses that period and its real allowance. Where there is not, it says "in the last 30 days" and tells you what you have left. Your figure moves when you cast, which is the thing you were telling us it did not do.

THE ONE I WENT LOOKING FOR AFTERWARDS IS WORSE THAN THE ONE YOU REPORTED. The same mistake — measuring against a cycle that does not run — was on the Billing pane twice, and one of them is embarrassing: the bar is capped at full but the sentence beside it is not, so on your own account (24,535 credits against a 5,000 "allowance") that pane has been reading "491% of this month's allowance left". Both are gone.

ALSO IN THESE FRAMES. "Frames made" is gone, and not because it was confusing — because it was false. It was counting charged operations, and on your account those are nineteen different things including "Mint package" and "Evidence package synchronization", neither of which makes a frame, while "Refresh views" makes several for one charge. You said not to keep a number nobody can name, so it went. The Refer a friend links were 16px against an 11px sentence and are 11px now. Bio is gone from Profile on your word — the field only; anything already written is still in your own data export. And Remove actually removes: I put a real picture on a test account, clicked it, and checked afterwards that the picture went back to the default AND the file left our storage rather than being left behind.

NOTHING HERE NEEDS A DECISION unless the last-30-days window is not what you want. If you would rather Usage showed all time, or the current calendar month with an honest label, say so and it is one line.

frames.caption: BEFORE — "Usage this month", credits used 0, "of 500,000 this month". The account behind this frame made 194 charged casts in the last 30 days.
AFTER — "Usage in the last 30 days", 7,895 used, and the note says what is left instead of an allowance that never renews. Two tiles, not three.
BEFORE — "Redeem a code" and "Who has joined" at 16px, towering over the row they sit on.
AFTER — both at 11px, the size of the sentence beside them, as your prototype draws them.
Profile — Remove is a real control beside Upload, and the Bio row is gone. Driven end to end: the picture returns to the account default and the file leaves storage.

eyeItems.title: You said the account menu is perfect - closed. Frames kept for reference.
eyeItems.question:
No question, a look and one correction you will probably enjoy.

WHAT CHANGED. Everything in the menu is now set from your prototype rather than nudged toward it. The avatar is gone from inside the menu - you just clicked it to open the thing, so drawing it again 30px below was costing the width. In its place the second line now reads "1,240 credits · Owner": the number in the typewriter face because it is measured, the words in the normal one. Every group is separated by a real line now instead of a barely-there one, the rows run edge to edge, and all seven rows carry an icon including Sign out - your own reversal, and you were right that half-and-half reads as an oversight.

THE CORRECTION, and it is about your section 3. You wrote that the menu should be 216px and "looks like ~240px" - about 15% too big. Measured on the shipped menu before I touched it: it was 200px. It was 16 pixels too NARROW, not 24 too wide. Two of your other three figures were already correct - the labels were 12px and the row padding was 8px, exactly as specified.

So your reading was right and your numbers were not. It DID read loose - because of the avatar block and a slightly oversized name, not because of its width. Every value comes off your prototype either way, which is what you asked for. I am telling you because a wrong number left standing is how a future brief inherits it.

frames.caption: BEFORE, dark. The avatar repeated inside the menu, a bare "1,240 credits", groups divided by almost nothing, and rows inset from the edge. 200px wide.

AFTER, dark, same account. 216px. No avatar, "1,240 credits · Owner" with the number in mono, real lines between the groups, rows edge to edge, and the Admin and Moderation glyphs are your set's now rather than borrowed ones.
AFTER, light. Included because the thin separators are the part most likely to disappear on white - last night's specimen was a bar whose track was technically there and invisible.

In context under the chip, dark. Worth a glance for one thing: the credits chip in the bar says 1,240 and the menu says it again. Your own brief argued that pairing it with the role earns the repeat. This is that judgement, rendered.

eyeItems.title: You answered the Usage type question - prototype, 19px, normal face - and it is built. New frames below.
eyeItems.question:
Two things worth your eye, and one of them is a real question.

THE LOOK. These are the panes as they ship, photographed in the running app in both themes. Usage is the one you enumerated: one bordered card, three columns, each column stacking. Storage is a card with its own label and the note under the bar. Security has every row as its own card with Delete account tinted red.

THE QUESTION, and it is small. On the Usage card, the three numbers are in the typewriter face at 22px, because your card said mono and your brief says "values in mono; they are measured numbers." Your PROTOTYPE draws them in the normal face at 19px. I went with your card and the brief - two artifacts against one - and wrote the disagreement into the code so it is one line to reverse. If the numbers read too big or too typewritery beside everything else, say so and it goes back to 19 and the normal face.

One thing you may notice in the frames that is NOT a defect: the account shown is the test bot, so the plan says Studio and the numbers are its numbers, not yours.

frames.caption: DARK, the Usage card as it ships now. The three numbers are 19px in the normal face, exactly as your prototype draws them - they were 22px in the typewriter face until your answer.
frames.arm: usage numbers after your ruling, dark

frames.caption: LIGHT, the same card. The zeros are real for the test account this was photographed on - it has a balance and has never spent. It is NOT evidence about the zero you reported on your own account, which is a separate problem and is card #387.
frames.arm: usage numbers after your ruling, light

eyeItems.title: You judged the cog and said it is now correct - closed, and the same gear is on your account menu tonight
eyeItems.question: No question this time, only a look - you already gave the verdict and this is it built. What you said: "the cog is incorrect its a star or sun it should be a cog like in the top bar profile drop down menu." You were right, and it was not a matter of taste. The rail's cog and the sun in your top bar were literally the same drawing: a circle with eight straight lines coming off it at even angles, differing only in how big the circle was. Two names, one picture, four inches apart on the same screen. It is now the gear your own profile dropdown draws - the same one, copied rather than re-drawn by hand, because you pointed at a mark on your screen and a near-miss would have given you a THIRD gear instead of an answer. The frames put the two side by side at 8x so you can see they are now different things. If the gear reads heavy or blurry at real size, say so - it is one key back.

frames.caption: DARK, magnified 8x from the real render. LEFT is the rail's settings gear as it ships now. RIGHT is your top bar's theme toggle, untouched. The right-hand one is also what the LEFT one used to be - same construction, slightly different size - which is the whole of what you spotted.
LIGHT, the same pair. Included because a stroke that holds on black can fill in on white, and the gear has more line in it than anything else on that rail.
The whole rail, dark, so the gear is judged BESIDE its neighbours rather than on its own. A glyph can look right alone and wrong in a row - this is the row.

eyeItems.title: Two small things you asked for, side by side - the cog, and Invite lighting up
eyeItems.question: One question and it is only about the cog. You asked for a cogwheel and you have one, but it is eight spokes around a circle - and the icon you were replacing, the one you rejected months ago, you rejected in these words: "eight teeth plus an inner circle, which mushes into a blurred ring at 16px". So the thing I have put in its place is, described plainly, eight teeth and an inner circle. It survives the small size for a different reason - thin separate strokes rather than a filled gear outline - and to my eye it reads clearly. But that is a judgement about a picture, and yours is the one that counts. The frames are magnified 8x so you can see the actual pixels rather than a re-drawing. If it reads as a blur at real size, say so and it is one key back. Invite needs no question, only a look: resting on the left, hovered on the right.

frames.caption: THE COG, dark, magnified 8x from the real 16px render. Left is what was there - two horizontal rails with a handle on each, which is the standard drawing of a filter. Right is what ships. This is the pair your question is about.
The same pair in the light theme. Both were driven in the running app, not assumed from the file.
INVITE, dark, magnified 4x. Resting on the left, pointed at on the right - the dashed circle goes to full white. Your original value for it, unchanged since you asked for it.
Invite in the light theme: the same lift, dashed grey to near-black. Keyboard focus does the same thing, so it is not mouse-only.

eyeItems.title: Your account, rebuilt - six frames, both themes
eyeItems.question: Two things I would rather you ruled on than me. First: are the six pages the right six? Referrals is a block inside Billing rather than a seventh page, because a page you visit twice a year should not own a permanent row - that is your brief's own reasoning and I followed it, but it is a judgement. Second: Members, Notifications and all three Security rows are dead on purpose, because there is nothing behind them. Together that is a lot of greyed-out surface in one window. Your own stub rule warns about the RATIO - four dead rows out of six reads as broken rather than as coming. Look at Members and Notifications and tell me whether it reads as honest or as empty. If it reads as empty, the fix is to hide those two pages until they work, and that is one line each.

frames.caption: Billing: what you are on, what is left, your referral link, your invoices - and the two buttons that used to be two more windows.
Profile in the light theme. Your email is shown and greyed with the reason beside it rather than hidden - hiding it makes people think the account has no email.
Members: designed in full, every control dead, and it says so. This is the section you named as the example.

Add credits, sitting over the plan window. Every number on it is worked out from four figures the server returns, so the date it names and the amount it charges cannot disagree.

eyeItems.title: The red box, before and after - and the one change I made that you did not ask for
eyeItems.question: Two questions, and the second is the one I would rather you ruled on than me. First, the simple one: in the before and after pair, is the quiet grey rule the mark you meant by "the quieter mark"? Second, and this is the honest part - fixing your word-picker turned up the same defect in casting studio V2 itself, the surface you told me to copy. Three of its rows were drawing the red ring AND the quiet rule at the same time, so the convention its own code describes has never been on your screen. I fixed those three in the same change rather than leave your word-picker looking different from the thing it was told to match. That IS a visible change to casting, under keyboard focus only, and casting is the one surface you have said is properly designed - so if you would rather it stayed as it was, say so and it is one line each. Money: zero. No render, no credit, no text call.

frames.caption: BEFORE, dark, 1440x900. The word-picker open on "athletic" with the keyboard on the first option - this is the red box you photographed. Worth knowing: that ring is not even the rule written on this row. The row’s own rule was losing a priority tie and never drew at all, so what you were looking at was the app-wide focus colour leaking through.

AFTER, dark, same page, same keystroke. The thin grey rule around "athletic" is casting V2’s own convention for a row: the border carries focus, nothing rings inside it. Same position, same panel, same keyboard.

The card menu, dark, with the keyboard walked onto "Rename" - the shape you said was already correct. It shows no mark at all until a keyboard reaches it, which is exactly why it read clean to you and the word-picker did not; now that a keyboard IS on it, it speaks the same quiet language. This panel needed the OPPOSITE fix, and writing it the same way as its sibling silently broke it - caught by pressing a key, not by reading.

eyeItems.title: The two shapes, one behaviour — the word-picker in dark, the card menu in light
eyeItems.question: Nothing here needs judging against a number — it needs your eye on whether the panels still look right. One thing DID move and I want to be straight about it: the word-picker in the casting sentence now sits 3.44px lower. It used to be positioned against an invisible box around the word rather than the word itself, so its “9px gap” was really 9px minus whatever the typeface added on that line; it is 9px from the word now, at any type size. That is smaller than an eye can judge without a ruler, and there is no before-picture to compare against because the panel's old position was only ever a measurement — so the question is simply: does it look right where it sits?

The 12px it hangs to the left of the word is unchanged and measured so; the gap under the word is the 3.44px that moved. LIGHT, 1440x900. The card menu open on the same page — the other shape, on the same behaviour underneath. eyeItems.title: Your cyborg, eight ways — and one thing in every single frame is on the wrong side
eyeItems.question: Two questions, and the second is the one I would not decide for you. RIGHT COLUMN - two ordinary faces that have eyebrows. The overlay is on their eyebrows. Correct, both times.

LEFT COLUMN - two creatures with no eyebrow hair at all. Instead of "there are none", the studio painted eyebrows onto the bare ridge above the eyes. Why it matters in the product: this is the step that checks our own work after you ask for something to be taken off. When it wrongly says the thing is still there, we do not update the face's record - so the next edit paints it back on. You would get what you asked for once, then lose it.

This does NOT need a verdict from you. The decision it feeds is on the card below it, and my recommendation there has changed because of it.

eyeItems.title: ANSWERED — you said top crop on both, and the Delete dialog now takes it (#198 closed)
eyeItems.question:
A small one, and the only reason it needs your eye is that the obvious fix would have moved faces.

WHAT WAS WRONG. Sign and Delete are the same dialog with different words. The instruction that sizes the portrait in that dialog had a typo-shaped mistake in it — it was written to point at the picture, and it pointed one level off, so for as long as it has existed it has applied to NOTHING. The Sign portrait was being sized by the browser's default and then simply cut off at the bottom by the frame around it. The Delete portrait, by an accident of where its grey-out lives, DID get the instruction. So the same face in the same dialog shell was being cropped two different ways depending on which button you pressed.

It has never looked broken, and that is exactly why it survived: our own renders are all the same shape, so cutting the bottom off and cropping properly happen to land in the same place.

WHY IT NEEDED YOU. Making the instruction work as written centres the crop — which slides the face about 27 pixels. That is a change to two dialogs you have already accepted, so the card for this was filed rather than fixed, months ago, waiting for someone to put frames in front of you.

WHAT I DID INSTEAD. Anchored the crop to the TOP, which is where the browser was already cutting. Then measured it rather than trusting my own eye: the Delete portrait is pixel-for-pixel identical, not one pixel of 57,620 changed. The Sign portrait is not quite byte-identical — the picture is scaled by a very slightly different route now — but there is no movement in it, and I proved that by ALSO building the version that does move and measuring both through the same instrument. That is the third panel.

⚠ AND THE THIRD PANEL IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH SEEING. Centred is exactly what your DELETE dialog does today. On a standard 1024x1536 render the Delete portrait shows source rows 128 to 1408 — it takes 128 pixels off the top and 128 off the bottom — while the Sign portrait shows rows 0 to 1280, dropping 256 off the bottom and nothing off the top. So panel three is not a mock-up of a bad idea; it is a photograph of the other half of your own product, and the gap between panel one and panel three is the bug.

THE QUESTION: the left and middle panels should look the same to you. Do they? It measured a fix, found that the FASTER version of that fix quietly switches the check off, and deliberately shipped nothing. Tonight that fix is in - the safe version - and the check runs in 29 seconds instead of 119.

The part worth knowing is the second half. The thing this check is meant to catch is the studio's own map going wrong. To catch that it builds the map twice and compares. Nothing in the test suite had ever checked that the COMPARISON works - so if someone had accidentally deleted it, every test would still have passed. We proved that: we broke the comparison on purpose, two different ways, and all eighteen existing tests stayed green.

pipeline.title: Found why the safety check that guards every change takes two minutes - and why the obvious fix would have broken it (#233)
pipeline.note: Every change the team makes has to pass a set of automatic checks before it can go anywhere. One of those checks keeps failing for the wrong reason - not because anything is wrong, but because it runs out of time when the computer is busy. Two shifts had already reported it and both deliberately left it alone, because raising the time limit without knowing WHY it is slow is how a slow tool becomes permanent. Tonight I found out why. The check rebuilds a full picture of the codebase 22 times in a row, from exactly the same unchanged files, and about 83 per cent of each rebuild is one expensive step repeated for nothing. Reusing that one step instead of redoing it takes the check from 119 seconds to 19 - and all 17 of its own tests still pass. But the finding that matters is the near-miss: there is an even faster version, 7 seconds, which is what anyone would reach for first - and I measured that it SILENTLY SWITCHES OFF one of the safety checks inside it. I proved that by deliberately breaking the tool and watching the fast version report everything as fine. It would have shipped looking like the bigger win. Nothing was changed tonight: this file sits on the path every change goes through, and your Fable reviewer is still down, so it is written up and queued rather than shipped.

We have a check that stops anyone deleting code without a written decision about it. So the honest summary is: a check we rely on to tell us what is dead can report "all clear" for something nobody has touched in months, purely because something else shares its name. Nothing was deleted; both are written down with reasons. Fixing the check properly means re-taking every reading it has ever produced, which is a night of its own — filed as #274 rather than half-done tonight.

problems.title: Your Fable allowance is still out - about five days now, and tonight's red tick was NOT one of them
problems.detail:
The reviewer is back and #219 closed on your word. Proven rather than assumed: it ran on both of tonight's changes and returned full written verdicts, one of which found a real miss of mine.

— resolved 2 September (#439). The original reading is kept below so the history stays readable.

Still down. Every pull request since has merged on the machine gate alone, which your standing rule allows for a change that touches no money and no login path.

TONIGHT IS DIFFERENT AND WORTH ONE PARAGRAPH, because the page would otherwise show you another red tick and you would reasonably read it as another refusal. Tonight's change edits the reviewer's own settings file. The reviewer refuses to run on any change to its own settings - that is a deliberate safety rule on their side, not ours - so our gate deliberately turns the tick RED rather than letting it go green over a review that never happened. I read the action log rather than the tick, and it says in its own words: "NO VERDICT - the reviewer cannot run on its own change". The change was reviewed by hand instead and that review is written on the pull request, which is what that rule asks for.

The thing that is easy to get backwards, and it is why the log gets read every time: a RED review tick does NOT mean the reviewer rejected the change. It means NO REVIEW WAS PRODUCED. A real verdict rides a GREEN tick, as a comment.

Opus is answering fine on the same machine and the same login - it ran tonight's whole shift. It is your Fable 5 allowance specifically, and N1 stays open until it can do the milestone read.

problems.title: Last night's briefing was written and never reached your page - and the fact you are reading this is the proof it is fixed
problems.detail: Edition 93 was finished and pushed at 10:07 yesterday morning and you never saw it. Railway built the new version perfectly - the build log is clean and the finished image was uploaded at 00:13 - and then the container that was meant to run it never started. It produced not one line of output for twenty-nine minutes and was stopped. The deploy ceremony watched for thirty minutes, refused to report a deploy it had not seen finish, and exited with an error, which is exactly what it is for. It was not our change: the only difference between that version and the one that was running is eleven lines of the briefing file itself. Your studio was never affected - production stayed healthy on the previous build the whole time, no credits, no renders, nothing a customer could touch. The one cost was that a night's journal sat where you could not read it, and the single thing needing your answer was already on the page you could see. Tonight's push carries both editions' news. If this ever happens twice in a row it stops being a stall and becomes an infrastructure problem worth raising.

problems.title: The deploy check refused three nights running over a file that is out of date by design — FIXED
problems.detail: Our deploy runs a check that our internal architecture map is up to date. Part of that check compared a generated web page (docs/architecture/index.html) against what the source would produce now — but that page is deliberately excluded from the project's saved files, so it only ever holds whatever the last person to run the generator locally produced. Merge somebody's work, pull it down, and the page is stale immediately and permanently. The check refused; regenerating cleared it while showing no change at all, which is what made it look like a ghost. Diagnosed at the artifacts by the previous shift, fixed here (#195): a freshness verdict is only a finding where there is a saved copy somebody could review. No customer effect at any point — the only cost was shift time, roughly half an hour a night for three nights.

problems.title: Quiet shifts were deploying — FIXED: the rite now refuses a briefing whose only change is a quiet journal line
problems.detail: Two quiet shifts this morning (09:45, 10:23) each ran a full production deploy for one journal line, after the standing orders had said a quiet shift ships nothing. The runner backs off 30 minutes after a quiet shift, and the deploy rite now refuses the quiet edition itself (PR #160) — so the order is a mechanical guard, not a sentence. No customer effect. (issue #159, closed)

problems.title: The deploy rite could push a script to main that the test gate rejects — FIXED: the rite now runs the script checks on the exact commit before it pushes
problems.detail: Two patrol helper scripts rode to main with briefing e39 and neither ended the way the script guard requires, so the guard was red on main for a night and the next pull request inherited the failure. No customer effect. Fixed (PR #157, foreman-42): before pushing, the rite checks out the commit into a throwaway folder and runs every suite that checks our scripts there — eight at today's tree, found by reading the suites rather than by a list — and refuses the push on any red. Proven green on today's tree (6 s) and red on a deliberate bad commit. (issue #152, closed)

problems.title: The automatic code review was failing in under a second (#114) — it healed by itself once the account's usage window passed; two full reviews ran on PR #123 today
problems.detail: Every substantial pull request gets an automatic Claude review before it merges. It has now failed four times in a row since 09:10 (each within a second, no message). I reran it with full logging: the login token IS valid — a small helper call was billed to it in the same run — and the tool version is unchanged; only the big-model (Fable) call dies, every time. Two explanations are left: your subscription's usage window was hit (the 08:59 review alone cost $2.85 and your own sessions share the plan), which heals itself; or the account's access to that model changed, which would be yours to look at. One rerun after about 14:00 today tells them apart; the next shift does it. Meanwhile merges still run unreviewed by the machine — this shift reviewed its own pull request by hand and posted the review on it before merging. Fifth instance on this shift's PR (11:05), same shape. The deciding rerun (five hours after the first failure) is still ahead.

problems.title: Shift processes dying before their close — cause found and the machine stamp is live (#101 done)
problems.detail: The 07:00 shift's report said the register was merged, your page was shipped and its workspace cleaned; at 07:17 none of those had happened — the process died mid-close and left a template placeholder where the deploy receipt goes. Nothing reached you wrong (this edition is the first one after it) and the register is now genuinely merged, still switched off. The class: a report written before the acts. Fix: the shift runner will stamp every close after the shift exits — receipt present or not, each "merged" checked against GitHub — so a dead shift cannot leave "done" standing (#101). Until that lands, every shift reads the previous one at the artifacts, which is what caught this. UPDATE 08:28: it happened twice more on one patrol — the Warden's first two processes each died after pushing but before merging, reporting, or writing your page. Nothing was lost (the third seat found the work at GitHub and finished it), but #101 moves up: it is the next maintenance build once your register word is handled. UPDATE 09:25: the cause is found at the logs — a shift ends its turn to wait for a background notification ("waiting for the gate result"), and a headless shift's process exits the moment its turn ends, so it never comes back. It hit the Machinist twice this morning (both seats died within a minute of writing that sentence). Two fixes: the shift runner now writes a machine stamp under every report after the process is gone — receipt present, placeholder absent, every "merged" checked against GitHub — and marks an unverified close in red for the next shift to read first (#101, proven on fixtures: a false claim is flagged, a true one is not); and the standing orders now say to wait in the foreground, never by ending the turn.

problems.title: The OpenRouter account is nearly empty again — $7.70 left, about three days at the current rate, and at zero the studio visibly stops taking briefs
problems.detail:
OpenRouter tops itself up. A balance is a reading on the deploy receipt, never a problem — your words, 2 September: "open router auto tops up i never want to see it as an issue appear again". The alarm that produced this row was removed in #440, and the standing orders now say a provider balance is never written here again.

— resolved 2 September (#439). The original reading is kept below so the history stays readable.

OpenRouter is the text engine behind every roll and refine: it reads each brief and each edit before anything renders. It is LOW: $7.70 remaining of $260 granted, $252.30 spent — re-read at the endpoint myself at 22:51Z on 29 Aug, not inherited.

Twenty-five minutes after the previous reading it is the same figure, and that is what it should be: nothing was rolling. The account's own daily counter says $3.59 went out on 29 Aug, so it is spending normally. (Editions 118-120 said this number "had not moved for a third night running" and made the account look frozen; that was corrected in edition 121 and the correction holds — the shifts run back to back through one night and three readings inside two hours were each written up as a separate night.)

The original point stands and is unchanged: money goes out, and the GRANTED figure has not risen since 27 Aug, when a $10 top-up did land (250 to 260). Whatever tops this account up is topping up less than it burns. Runway at this rate is about two days.

What happens at zero is DRIVEN rather than remembered (30 Aug, foreman-111): an EDIT is refused free — nobody charged, nobody can edit — and a ROLL is refused free too. Nobody loses credits; the studio visibly stops taking briefs.

fal (the image engine) is separate and tops itself up.
